title: US Seeks 293-Month Term for Nikhil Gupta in Pannun Murder-for-Hire Plot
excerpt: Prosecutors call Gupta a crucial participant in a foreign plot and ask for just over 24 years; his lawyers seek 12 years. Judge Victor Marrero sentences him on November 20.
body:
• US prosecutors have asked a New York federal court to sentence Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 293 months in prison — just over 24 years — for his role in the plot to assassinate Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York.
  • Gupta's lawyers have asked for 12 years, backing the Probation Department's recommendation, arguing he accepted responsibility and has no previous criminal record.
  • Gupta pleaded guilty in February 2026 to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering. The charges carry a combined maximum of 40 years.
  • Sentencing is scheduled for November 20 before US District Judge Victor Marrero in the Southern District of New York, who is not bound by either side's request.

US prosecutors have asked a federal court in New York to impose a sentence of 293 months — just over 24 years — on Nikhil Gupta, the Indian national who pleaded guilty to plotting the assassination of Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun on American soil. The request, made in a sentencing filing dated November 13, sets up a wide gap with the defence, which has asked the court for a 12-year term ahead of sentencing on November 20.

"The defendant's conduct was as brutal as it was brazen. He was a crucial participant in a foreign plot to execute a US citizen on US soil," prosecutors wrote in the filing, asking the court to impose a sentence that "sends a message that the violent silencing of voices in this country will not be tolerated."

Two very different asks

Gupta's defence team, in its own sentencing memorandum to the US District Court for the Southern District of New York, urged the court to impose the 12-year term recommended by the Probation Department. His lawyers argued that he deserved leniency because he had accepted responsibility and had no previous criminal record.

In a letter to Judge Victor Marrero, the 55-year-old expressed remorse and spoke about his struggles with alcoholism. "I wish I could turn back time to 2023 and undo my mistakes. Now, when I look back, I don't even recognise the man I had become," he wrote.

The defence has portrayed Gupta as a man who acted under pressure from Vikash Yadav, the Indian intelligence official US authorities accuse of directing the plot. According to the defence, Gupta was approached by Yadav after men claiming to be Gujarat Police personnel visited his home in India, and Yadav assured him a "fake case" against him was "all clear."

Prosecutors dismissed the plea for leniency. They maintained that Gupta played a central role in the conspiracy over an extended period, argued he was driven by financial gain — including promised profits from weapons sales and drug shipments — and rejected the claim that alcohol had impaired his judgement, pointing to planning and coordination over several weeks.

The target's account

Pannun, a US citizen and legal counsel for Sikhs for Justice, was designated an "individual terrorist" by India in July 2020. In his victim impact statement, he sought the maximum sentence on every count, saying the plot had forced him to live with security for 1,200 days and prevented him from meeting legal clients in person.

How the case reached sentencing

According to the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York, Gupta was recruited by an Indian government employee, identified in court papers as CC-1, a self-described "senior field officer" responsible for "security management" and "intelligence." In May 2023, CC-1 asked Gupta to arrange the murder of a US citizen of Indian origin living in New York City. Gupta asked a man he believed was a criminal associate — in fact a confidential source working with the Drug Enforcement Administration — to carry out the killing for $100,000, and $15,000 in cash was delivered to the source in Manhattan as an advance.

Gupta was arrested in the Czech Republic on June 30, 2023, and extradited to the United States on June 14, 2024. On February 13, 2026, he pleaded guilty before Judge Marrero to murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering, and to conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire. US Attorney Jay Clayton said at the plea that Gupta "admitted today that he plotted to assassinate a U.S. citizen on American soil, at the direction of an Indian government employee."

India has denied any state involvement in the alleged plot. New Delhi said it took the US inputs seriously and formed a high-level enquiry committee in November 2023; in January 2025, the Ministry of Home Affairs said the panel had recommended legal action against an individual following its investigation.

What happens next

Judge Marrero will sentence Gupta on November 20, and is not bound by either side's request or the Probation Department's recommendation. The sentence will close Gupta's criminal case, though Pannun's separate civil lawsuit against Indian officials in the same court district continues.
